newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN CLAIMS FIRST GRAND PRIX VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FRENTZEN CLAIMS FIRST GRAND PRIX VICTORY.

text.p: Heinz-Harald Frentzen answered his critics in the best possible way when he beat off fellow German Michael Schumacher to win the San Marino Grand Prix on Sunday.
It earned Frentzen his first Grand Prix win in 52 races and also his first points of the season since controversially being recruited by the Williams team in place of world champion Damon Hill.
Frentzen held off a blistering challenge by Ferrari driver Schumacher in the closing laps to finish 1.2 seconds ahead of the twice world champion.
It was the first time two German drivers had filled the first two places in a Formula One race.

Frentzen has long lived in the shadow of Schumacher and had come in for increasing criticism after failing to gain a top six place in the opening three races of the season in what is recognised as the best car on the circuit.
The result lifted him into equal third in the title race with 10 points, behind team mate Jacques Villeneuve of Canada on 20 points and Schumacher on 14 after four of the season's 17 races.

Schumacher did his utmost to supply the local Italian fans with a Ferrari victory to celebrate on their 'home' circuit, but was forced to settle for second, one place ahead of team mate Eddie Irvine on Britain.

Villeneuve, who led the opening 26 laps after starting from his fourth successive pole position, lost the lead during the opening pit-stops. He was still third when gearbox trouble prevented him re-entering the race after his second pit-stop.

This left the way open for Italian Giancarlo Fisichella to prove his talent by claiming his first championship points in fourth place for Jordan, ahead of Frenchman Jean Alesi's Benetton and the McLaren of Mika Hakkinen of Finland.

The woeful season for Britain's defending champion Hill continued when electrical problems forced him to start from the pit lane in his Arrows and he then crashed out after only 11 laps when he collided with Shinji Nakano's Prost at the Variante Bassa.

Frentzen struggled for words afterwards, but said: "I am very happy. When I saw P1 on the board after my pitstops, I was happy and suprised. I thought I was coming in before Jacques, but when I saw he and Michael went in I pushed very hard for two laps to try and get an advantage and that is when I won it.

"I was a bit worried later on about my brakes because I did not want to experience another problem like the one in Melbourne and we had some intetesting conversations with the pit crew. Michael was right behind me and I had to concentrate and keep a rhythm. It feels great to win."
Schumacher congratulated Frentzen, a former Mercedes-Benz junior team mate in their early careers. He blamed Sauber driver Nicola Larini of Italy for slowing him up and causing him to brake hard.
"This meant I had to stop and pit because I had flat-spotted my tyres," he said.
Villeneuve, winner of the previous two races in South America, had made a perfect getaway from the grid on a drying circuit after a morning of showers following overnight rain.

Schumacher also made a strong start and muscled his way past Frentzen in the rush towards Tamburello to claim second place but Villeneuve looked well in command over the opening laps as he reeled off a series of fastest lap times.
Schumacher and Frentzen could only struggle to keep with him and by the end of the sixth lap he was more than a second clear.
Austrian Gerhard Berger in a Benetton made a sad exit from his 200th Grand Prix when he spun off on the fifth lap at Acque Minerale.
Frentzen continued to battle to find a way past Schumacher for second place but Irvine moved up the field when he overtook Frenchman Olivier Panis's Prost at Piratella on lap 18.

There followed a frantic shuffling of postions as Ralf Schumacher coasted into the pits to retire in his Jordan and then Briton Johnny Herbert in a Sauber, who had run powerfully in fifth following a brilliant start from seventh on the grid, went off on lap 19.

Villeneuve remained ahead of the field but when the pit-stops began -- with Schumacher first in after lap 24 -- everything began to change with Frentzen, driving with huge determination, emerging in front of Schumacher and Villeneuve.
Schumacher battled hard to close the gap but Frentzen proved resiliant while Villeneuve fell further behind before retiring.
